title: Drool Kaomoji (￣﹃￣): Copy & Paste Drooling Text Faces
meta_description: Copy and paste drool kaomoji: hungry faces like (￣﹃￣) and (๑´ڡ`๑), lovestruck drooling like (♡﹃♡), sleepy (´ρ`) and drooling cats and bears.
hero_tagline: Mouths hanging open over food, a crush or something too cute to handle. One click copies the face.
intro: Drool kaomoji draw the mouth as an open curve with something hanging from it. ﹃ is the most common: a vertical bracket that reads as a slack mouth with a line of drool, so (￣﹃￣) is someone staring at a plate. ڡ, an Arabic letter, looks like a tongue curling out to lick the lips, which makes it the go-to for food that already tastes good. ρ, the Greek letter rho, hangs below the line like a dribble and turns up in sleepy faces. Change the eyes and the reason changes: ♡ eyes are drooling over a person, ✪ eyes over something shiny. These are text characters, so they paste into any field that accepts Unicode text.

sections.label: Classic Drool
sections.intro: The ﹃ mouth with different eyes. Flat ￣ eyes stare, closed ˘ eyes daydream.

sections.label: Hungry & Food
sections.intro: For a menu photo, a friend's dinner or the last slice. ♨ is steam rising off something hot.

sections.label: Crush
sections.intro: Heart eyes plus an open mouth: the face for a photo of someone attractive.

sections.label: Sleepy Drool
sections.intro: The ρ mouth dribbles while the face nods off or zones out.

sections.label: Animal Drool
sections.intro: Animal faces with the same drool mouth, for pet photos and cute-overload moments.

faq.a: ﹃ is a presentation form of a corner bracket used in vertically set Chinese and Japanese text. Turned into a mouth, its hook hangs down like drool, which is why it became the standard drooling mouth.

faq.q: Why do some food kaomoji use ڡ?
faq.a: ڡ is an Arabic letter whose curl looks like a tongue poking out to lick the lips. Faces like (๑´ڡ`๑) mean something tastes good, while ﹃ faces mean you want it and have not had it yet.
Usually sleepy or dazed. The ρ hangs below the line like a dribble from a slack mouth, so it suits nodding off or zoning out more than craving food.
